Learn more Description Live Radar: Rare Level 4 Severe Weather Threat for Virginia SEVERE WEATHER THREAT MONDAY — Damaging wind gusts, large hail, and tornadoes possible Monday will be windy and warm with highs in the 70s and wind gusts over 30 mph. There will be some showers and the chance for thunderstorms during the morning, especially late morning and midday. A few of these storms may be severe. A line of more powerful storms will move in from the west as a cold front approaches during the afternoon. There is a moderate risk (level 4 out of 5) of severe weather. The main threat will be damaging wind gusts, possibly exceeding 70 mph. Some large hail over 1" in diameter is also possible. There is a risk of multiple tornadoes, some of which could produce winds over 100 mph. Due to the dynamics in place, these could be "long track" tornadoes, meaning they would stay on the ground for an extended period of time. Storms should exit eastern Virginia by around 8 p.m. Final rain totals may exceed an inch in some areas.
